Definition: perhaps from G2095 and G5087; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once:--anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway.
BiblicalUsage: euthýs is a plain word for straight, right. In Matthew 3:3, the text says "make his paths straight." In Mark 1:3, the text says "make his paths straight."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading euthýs this way, I believe truth is not whatever we feel; it is what God has said, and it stands. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Baptism of Jesus; The Last Supper
